summary.name: Risograph Printing, in the Printmaking and Craft Materials category. Provenance is explicit: the source directly names this style.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit risograph look: two or three inks on natural paper, with overprints creating extra tones. Controlled grain, dots and slight registration offsets are added without sacrificing text. Registration errors stay stable across frames rather than jittering.
summary.suitableUses: The source says to use risograph alone for posters and illustrations where two-ink overprint is the identity. Hybrids suit typography-led work such as event promos, zine-like posts, editorial title cards and illustrated explainers. Other formats are inferred, not stated.
summary.limitations: Two-color contrast checks do not guarantee readability over grain, texture, video or animated effects, so recheck composited frames. Coral reaches only 3.242:1 on paper, so it is decorative, not body text. Gradients are disabled. Simulated appearance is not proof of physical print production.
summary.palette: This is an authored suggestion, not a supplied palette. Background #F4EBD8 is paper, foreground #254687 is blue ink, and accent_1 #D95664 is coral ink. Exactly two independent inks are allowed, and overprint is the only third tone. Blue on paper at 7.69:1 is the approved text pair. Task-supplied exact colors override these tokens.
summary.motionAndInteraction: The style directs revealing color separations and swapping printed forms, with registration held stable rather than jittering per frame. Optional motion references 012 and 015 give chapter and story structure. References 037 to 039 offer phrase, punctuation and ink-burst actions, adapted to two inks. Reference 040 is optional and has no review evidence. Video runs on composition time. Scroll or pointer behavior applies only to interactive delivery, and reduced motion shows the completed state.
summary.audio: Audio is unspecified by the style, which forbids assigning a fixed genre, tempo, voice or mandatory layer. Propose audio from the topic and objective, honoring user input first. Restrained sound accents or intentional silence may suit ink reveals and reading holds. No audio was inspected, so beat synchronization is unverified. Voiceover must not compete with copy.
summary.assetRequirements: The source supplies no copy, artwork, fonts or paper textures. Task-supplied exact wording, approved artwork and local fonts must be loaded before rendering. Paper, grain and halftone textures must be generated or authorized. Do not invent product copy or brand marks. Pillow or Sharp may preprocess images, and Python may manage frame sequences.
summary.combinations: Style-093 (kinetic type) supplies headline sequencing: plates reveal blue then coral with constant misregistration, and overprint marks stressed words. Style-028 (flat vector) supplies explainer figures separated into two plates, with its own palette and gradients dropped. Both collapse into the two inks. Supporting styles must follow the same two-ink and stable-registration rules.
summary.productionApproach: Select SVG as the style renderer for ink separations, grain and registration offsets. Use GSAP as the paused, seekable motion owner, with Motion optional, and keep one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the default pipeline for assembly, timing, sync and export; Remotion is only a verified fallback. Verify forward, backward and direct seeks.
